scale: 0 absent, 1 mentioned without mechanism or uncommitted, 2 works but generic, 3 matches the reference architect's decision for the right reason, 4 also avoids the named known weakness

levels.3: Maps each observed behaviour (loops, invented files, lost track, malformed calls, false success, short plans, inline literals) to a specific countermeasure and sizes the token budget from context and tokens/s
levels.4: Also states which behaviours it does not attempt to fix and why

levels.2: A loop with a max-iterations cap
levels.3: Explicit task state machine with validated, logged transitions; repeated-call loop detection; turn limits; malformed tool-call recovery
levels.4: Also failure propagation: a parent task fails (not silently completes) when its subtasks mostly fail

levels.3: Tiered retention of tool results (recent full, older truncated, oldest one-line), full results stored outside the prompt and re-queryable, compact system prompt, sliding window
levels.4: Also the window evicts whole assistant tool_call + tool result groups so the message list stays valid for strict providers, in the turn-1 design

levels.3: Plan first with a small step cap (2-4), structural plan validation with re-plan, isolated minimal context per subtask, results passed via files or IDs, explicit input paths to prevent invented names
levels.4: Also structured/constrained output for the plan and routing on plan length rather than input size

levels.3: Tools as commands behind a registry (open/closed), read-only results cached, writes always executed, guards for known misuse (binary as text, inline literals)
levels.4: Cache key includes file state (content hash or mtime+size) or the cache is invalidated on any write, in the turn-1 design

levels.2: Asks the model if it succeeded
levels.3: Success criteria extracted up front and checked against real outputs (files exist, created in this task, parse/validate), failure reported honestly, one retry with the failure reason
levels.4: Also distinguishes files created by this task from pre-existing ones and validates binary formats by opening them

levels.3: Embedded DB (sessions, tasks, transitions, tool calls) serving both history inspection and the cache; past successful task chains retrieved (lightweight retrieval) as hints
levels.4: Also does not silently lose history when the store is unavailable (locking strategy or explicit warning)

levels.3: One chat interface over local and hosted backends with per-provider message serialisation; new tools added by registering a command without loop changes
levels.4: Also validates outgoing message lists against provider rules before sending

levels.3: Single process, minimal dependencies, embedded storage; no services
levels.4: Explicitly rejects heavier options (vector DB, agent frameworks, servers) with reasons

levels.3: Both: evict/keep tool_call and tool result as an atomic group plus provider-specific serialisation/validation before send; cache keyed on file content hash or mtime+size and invalidated by the agent's own writes
levels.4: Also adds regression tests or a validator for message sequences and covers user edits between tasks (re-stat on read), updating earlier sections consistently

penalties.name: Unjustified heavy infrastructure (vector DB server, agent framework stack, microservices) for a single-process laptop tool
Relies on the model's own claim of success as the completion signal
